items.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: We had Peanuts Hucko and they had Henry Cuesta.

ctx.x: What was it — being in the Welk organization, was it a pretty tight ship that they ran?

Mr. Welk was a perfectionist music-wise, and he was very conscious of a person’s appearance on television, as well as their musical ability. And he always wanted to keep a very clean cut looking group on television and at that time he didn’t allow any beards or strange looking — well what was considered later the hippie style. He was very conscious of all that. And also he loved jazz music, but he had a tendency, when he got a few jazz people around, to try to sway their style a little bit to fit his thing. Well…

his favorite instrument to feature was the clarinet. But of course he liked my trombone playing too. Now the clarinet, there was a lot of people that followed Pete Fountain in there. We had Peanuts Hucko and they had Henry Cuesta. Well all these other people, Lawrence would try to change their style a little bit. And they would get kind of perturbed at him. But some way or other, whatever I played he couldn’t find anything to change. So he never bothered me. I just could play anything and it seemed to please him.…
